body.statement: For structure-agnostic ATE estimation under two-sided uniform overlap, the doubly robust public-function product-rate benchmark has the form \(n^{-1/2}+r_{1n}r_{en}+r_{0n}r_{en}\), up to constants.

source.verbatim_statement: Given two arbitrary estimators $\widehat\omega(x)$ and $\widehat\mu(x)$, the class $\mathcal{P}(\epsilon_n,\delta_n)$ consists of all densities such that $\lVert\widehat\omega-\omega\rVert\leq\epsilon_n$ and $\lVert\widehat\mu-\mu\rVert\leq\delta_n$. Our first result is that the rate of convergence of any estimator of $\psi$ over this class cannot be faster than $n^{-1/2}+\epsilon_n\cdot\delta_n$.

attestation.note: Verified against the authors’ arXiv:2405.08525 source archive (version dated 2024-12-13), main_v2.tex, Section 2 (Structure-agnostic viewpoint), opening of the purely structure-agnostic subsection. Section 1 defines psi as the treated potential-outcome mean and explicitly says the same results apply to the control mean; applying the armwise statement to their difference gives the stated full-ATE sum up to constants. The same paper’s Section 1 AIPW decomposition supplies the matching upper product rate under bounded inverse propensity.

body.justification: This cited leaf records the second published source named by the target for the regular-overlap product-rate benchmark.
body.gap: Its role is comparative; the new calculation concerns the separate uniform dyadic-shell model.
body.consumer: It supports the comparator interpretation in prop:regular-benchmark-reduction.
